K<=100 bounds JavaScript row materialization; synchronous SQLite remains event-loop blocking; RSS/heap raw deltas are not peak memory.

No external API, webhook or MCP runtime integration.
Three comparable samples per tenant, whale skew and explicit read/write/storage cost model; no scaling/capacity claim.

costs.variables: N=60000 total; M=tenant rows; R=1621 ready rows; K<=100 returned; P=1 DB; C=1 sequential benchmark; Q=0 application queue
costs.before: Scan N and sort M tenant rows (comparison sort model O(M log M)); materialize M full records including 256-byte payloads. Each call has one query plus JS filter/slice/projection.
costs.after: Covering B-tree seek model O(log R+K) comparisons/entries with tenant-key comparison bytes; no temp sort observed. O(K) JS row storage, serialization O(output bytes). Native page cache/runtime memory is additional; total process peak is unmeasured.
costs.io: Plans support index-only access path and avoided payload projection. Logical access model is seek plus leaf entries; physical reads/writes, rows examined, locks and cache hits are unavailable.
costs.writes: Partial index maintains only ready rows; ready inserts/deletes, ordering keys and ready-status transitions add B-tree maintenance. No write throughput measured. Index build scans N, sorts keys, allocates pages and takes write lock; busy timeout 5000ms.

index.name: parcels_ready_tenant_order
index.sql: CREATE INDEX parcels_ready_tenant_order ON parcels(tenant,created_at DESC,id DESC) WHERE status='ready'

storage.note: 10 pages x 4096; includes stats/all allocation changes, not isolated index allocation or physical I/O.

costs.network: No network calls, fan-out or retries in query; local SQLite only.
costs.recovery: Rebuild cost includes table scan and ready-key sorting; measured one local index build only, no restore/RTO claim.

assumptions: Tenant is authorized by caller before this function; fixture contains no identity provider.
Single local file and no concurrent writer/load during microbenchmark.
Required order uses SQLite integer timestamp/id fields exactly as seeded.
limitations: First UTC request failed because Windows PowerShell lacks -AsUTC. The recorded interval starts at first successful UTC observation after initial reads; total turn elapsed is longer by an unmeasured initial interval. Trial stopped conservatively before 360 seconds.
Three descriptive samples per tenant are not independent production load trials; no p99, speedup ratio/confidence, SLO or horizontal capacity inferred.
OS cache uncontrolled; baseline/after use separate benchmark processes over the same database. DDL/ANALYZE warms data/index.
Elapsed values include benchmark materialized-row JSON encoding and application work, not isolated engine execution. Materialized JSON bytes are not physical I/O or network bytes.
RSS and heap deltas are raw noisy before/after snapshots, not peak or total memory bounds.
Engine rows examined, physical I/O, lock wait, cache hit counts, cold-cache behavior, OS ACL security, production load and write-amplification measurements unavailable.
Native SQLite emits ExperimentalWarning; retained in stderr. No downloads, external mutation, background helper or production deployment.
